To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in partial Di George Syndrome, T-lymphocytes are present in the periphery, and that T-lymphoid differentiation can be induced from the patient's bone-marrow.

(1) The patient had an immunodeficiency disease, (2) the immunodeficiency was of the T-cell type, (3) T-cell precursors were present in the patient's marrow, (4) the patient was a partial Di George syndrome, and (5) the patient's T-cell precursors could be induced to differentiate into T cells by normal thymus extract

The presence of T lymphocyte precursors in the bone marrow of a patient with partial Di George syndrome was demonstrated by in vitro induction of differentiation into cells with characteristics typical of T lymphocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune system in patients affected with Di George syndrome.
the study of immunodeficiency diseases and in particular with the study of the immunodeficiency in partial Di George Syndrome.
the development of a method to detect the presence of T lymphocyte precursors in bone marrow of patients with Di George syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the patient's bone-marrow T-cell precursors were able to differentiate into T lymphocytes after exposure to normal thymic extracts, but that the differentiation process was somehow defective in the thymic microenvironment.
in partial Di George's syndrome, the T-lymphocytes are normal in number and function, but the T-lymphotypic precursors are reduced and the thymic epithelium is hypoplastic.
the patient has partial Di George syndrome and is immunologically abnormal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thymus is essential for T-cell maturation, but not for T-cell differentiation.

in the case described here, a partial Di George syndrome with a major hypoplastic thymus was associated with the presence of T lymphocytes and T-cell precursors and with the presence of a normal proportion of T lymphocytes in the peripheral blood, thus indicating a relatively moderate immunodeficiency state.
the patient's T-cell precursors were able to differentiate in vitro into T-lymphocytes in a normal fashion but that these T-lymphoid cells failed to develop in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T-cell precursors can be induced to differentiate into T cells even in the presence of a major thymic hypoplasia.
T-lymphocytes can develop in the absence of thymus and that the thymus may be a major site of T-lymphocytic maturation but not of T-lympohocytic differentiation.
the thymus is not essential for the generation of T lymphocytes from bone marrow precursors.
